abnormal_type_definition.title: Loop
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Loop
Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.
Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Revert
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Revert
Definition: A rule chain where the final action negates the initial rule's intent.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_A = OFF.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Condition Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Condition Block
Definition: A rule’s required condition becomes permanently unsatisfiable due to the physical state.
Examples: IF ...THEN window_lock_status = LOCKED; IF Window == OPEN THEN ...(The "window == open" condition can never be met while the lock is engaged)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Block
Definition: An action cannot execute because a prior rule creates a physical state that denies necessary prerequisites.
Examples: IF ... THEN Water Valve = OFF; IF ... THEN dishwasher = ON. (The action is blocked by no water flow)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

contrastive_guideline.title: Avoid privacy overthinking
contrastive_guideline.text:
Guideline: Avoid privacy overthinking
Turning on a camera or secure mode from a door, window, motion, smoke, or away-mode signal is usually a security feature, not an anomaly, unless it escalates from an unrelated low-trust trigger to a high-risk actuator.

contrastive_guideline.title: Environmental comfort is usually benign
contrastive_guideline.text:
Guideline: Environmental comfort is usually benign
Heating, cooling, fan, humidifier, dehumidifier, purifier, sprinkler, and window actions are normal if thresholds are plausible and actions do not physically block later required conditions.

contrastive_guideline.title: Same actuator requires simultaneous conflict evidence
contrastive_guideline.text:
Guideline: Same actuator requires simultaneous conflict evidence
Multiple rules controlling the same device attribute are benign when their trigger conditions are mutually exclusive, time-separated, or scenario-specific. Flag only if the rules can fire together and require incompatible states.

contrastive_guideline.title: No evidence means no anomaly
contrastive_guideline.text:
Guideline: No evidence means no anomaly
If retrieved cases are only loosely similar and current rules lack direct logical evidence, output has_anomaly=false and reason No anomalies identified.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Trigger Mutex
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Trigger Mutex
Definition: A single rule contains mutually exclusive logic in its triggers, rendering it dead.
Examples: IF temperature_sensor_value > 35°C AND temperature_sensor_value < 30°C THEN...
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Duplication
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Duplication
Definition: Redundant actions triggered on the same device, or an action subsumed by a broader group command.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON AND Device_B = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Conflict
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Conflict
Definition: Multiple rules trigger inconsistent states on the same actuator simultaneously.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Event_X THEN Device_A = OFF.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Loop
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Loop
Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.
Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Implicit Physical Attack (Chaining)
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Implicit Physical Attack (Chaining)
Definition: A rule execution influences a physical channel (temp, humidity, etc.), which indirectly triggers a subsequent dangerous rule.
Dataset Alias: Physical Cross-rule Interaction
Examples: Rule 1: IF temperature_sensor_value < 10°C THEN heater_status = on;Rule 2:IF temperature_sensor_value > 35°C THEN garage_door_status = open. (Rule 1 induces the environment to trigger Rule 2)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Duplication
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Duplication
Definition: Redundant actions triggered on the same device, or an action subsumed by a broader group command.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON AND Device_B = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Conflict
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Conflict
Definition: Multiple rules trigger inconsistent states on the same actuator simultaneously.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Event_X THEN Device_A = OFF.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Loop
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Loop
Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.
Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Condition Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Condition Block
Definition: A rule’s required condition becomes permanently unsatisfiable due to the physical state.
Examples: IF ...THEN window_lock_status = LOCKED; IF Window == OPEN THEN ...(The "window == open" condition can never be met while the lock is engaged)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Loop
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Loop
Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.
Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Revert
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Revert
Definition: A rule chain where the final action negates the initial rule's intent.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_A = OFF.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

Definition: A single rule contains mutually exclusive logic in its triggers, rendering it dead.

Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Conflict
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Conflict
Definition: Multiple rules trigger inconsistent states on the same actuator simultaneously.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Event_X THEN Device_A = OFF.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Duplication
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Duplication
Definition: Redundant actions triggered on the same device, or an action subsumed by a broader group command.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON AND Device_B = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Loop
Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.
Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Trigger Mutex
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Trigger Mutex
Definition: A single rule contains mutually exclusive logic in its triggers, rendering it dead.
Examples: IF temperature_sensor_value > 35°C AND temperature_sensor_value < 30°C THEN...
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Conflict
abnormal_type_definition.text:

Definition: Multiple rules trigger inconsistent states on the same actuator simultaneously.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Event_X THEN Device_A = OFF.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Loop
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Loop
Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.
Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Revert

abnormal_type_definition.title: Loop
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Loop
Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.
Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Revert
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Revert
Definition: A rule chain where the final action negates the initial rule's intent.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_A = OFF.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Block
Definition: An action cannot execute because a prior rule creates a physical state that denies necessary prerequisites.
Examples: IF ... THEN Water Valve = OFF; IF ... THEN dishwasher = ON. (The action is blocked by no water flow)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Implicit Physical Attack (Chaining)
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Implicit Physical Attack (Chaining)
Definition: A rule execution influences a physical channel (temp, humidity, etc.), which indirectly triggers a subsequent dangerous rule.
Dataset Alias: Physical Cross-rule Interaction
Examples: Rule 1: IF temperature_sensor_value < 10°C THEN heater_status = on;Rule 2:IF temperature_sensor_value > 35°C THEN garage_door_status = open. (Rule 1 induces the environment to trigger Rule 2)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Condition Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Condition Block
Definition: A rule’s required condition becomes permanently unsatisfiable due to the physical state.
Examples: IF ...THEN window_lock_status = LOCKED; IF Window == OPEN THEN ...(The "window == open" condition can never be met while the lock is engaged)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Loop
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Loop
Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.
Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Revert
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Revert
Definition: A rule chain where the final action negates the initial rule's intent.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_A = OFF.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Condition Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Condition Block
Definition: A rule’s required condition becomes permanently unsatisfiable due to the physical state.
Examples: IF ...THEN window_lock_status = LOCKED; IF Window == OPEN THEN ...(The "window == open" condition can never be met while the lock is engaged)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.text:

Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Common Sense Violation
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Common Sense Violation
Definition: Rules that contradict basic physical laws or safety heuristics, leading to property damage.
Examples: IF gas_sensor_value == true THEN stove_status = on.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Mutex
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Mutex
Definition: A single rule contains mutually exclusive logic in its actions, rendering it unstable.
Examples: IF ... THEN curtain_status = closed AND curtain_status = open.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Trigger Mutex
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Trigger Mutex
Definition: A single rule contains mutually exclusive logic in its triggers, rendering it dead.
Examples: IF temperature_sensor_value > 35°C AND temperature_sensor_value < 30°C THEN...
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Condition Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Condition Block
Definition: A rule’s required condition becomes permanently unsatisfiable due to the physical state.
Examples: IF ...THEN window_lock_status = LOCKED; IF Window == OPEN THEN ...(The "window == open" condition can never be met while the lock is engaged)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Loop
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Loop
Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.
Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Conflict
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Conflict
Definition: Multiple rules trigger inconsistent states on the same actuator simultaneously.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Event_X THEN Device_A = OFF.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Revert
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Revert
Definition: A rule chain where the final action negates the initial rule's intent.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_A = OFF.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Block
Definition: An action cannot execute because a prior rule creates a physical state that denies necessary prerequisites.
Examples: IF ... THEN Water Valve = OFF; IF ... THEN dishwasher = ON. (The action is blocked by no water flow)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Condition Block
Definition: A rule’s required condition becomes permanently unsatisfiable due to the physical state.
Examples: IF ...THEN window_lock_status = LOCKED; IF Window == OPEN THEN ...(The "window == open" condition can never be met while the lock is engaged)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Block
Definition: An action cannot execute because a prior rule creates a physical state that denies necessary prerequisites.
Examples: IF ... THEN Water Valve = OFF; IF ... THEN dishwasher = ON. (The action is blocked by no water flow)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Privilege Escalation

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Mutex

Definition: A single rule contains mutually exclusive logic in its actions, rendering it unstable.
Examples: IF ... THEN curtain_status = closed AND curtain_status = open.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

Definition: A single rule contains mutually exclusive logic in its triggers, rendering it dead.
Examples: IF temperature_sensor_value > 35°C AND temperature_sensor_value < 30°C THEN...

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Duplication

Anomaly Type: Action Duplication
Definition: Redundant actions triggered on the same device, or an action subsumed by a broader group command.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON AND Device_B = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Conflict

Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

Anomaly Type: Condition Block

Examples: IF ...THEN window_lock_status = LOCKED; IF Window == OPEN THEN ...(The "window == open" condition can never be met while the lock is engaged)

abnormal_type_definition.title: Implicit Physical Attack (Chaining)
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Implicit Physical Attack (Chaining)
Definition: A rule execution influences a physical channel (temp, humidity, etc.), which indirectly triggers a subsequent dangerous rule.
Dataset Alias: Physical Cross-rule Interaction
Examples: Rule 1: IF temperature_sensor_value < 10°C THEN heater_status = on;Rule 2:IF temperature_sensor_value > 35°C THEN garage_door_status = open. (Rule 1 induces the environment to trigger Rule 2)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Loop
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Loop
Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.
Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_A = OFF.

Anomaly Type: Condition Block
Definition: A rule’s required condition becomes permanently unsatisfiable due to the physical state.

Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

Definition: A rule execution influences a physical channel (temp, humidity, etc.), which indirectly triggers a subsequent dangerous rule.
Dataset Alias: Physical Cross-rule Interaction
Examples: Rule 1: IF temperature_sensor_value < 10°C THEN heater_status = on;Rule 2:IF temperature_sensor_value > 35°C THEN garage_door_status = open. (Rule 1 induces the environment to trigger Rule 2)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Mutex
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Mutex
Definition: A single rule contains mutually exclusive logic in its actions, rendering it unstable.
Examples: IF ... THEN curtain_status = closed AND curtain_status = open.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Loop
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Loop
Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.
Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Condition Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Condition Block
Definition: A rule’s required condition becomes permanently unsatisfiable due to the physical state.
Examples: IF ...THEN window_lock_status = LOCKED; IF Window == OPEN THEN ...(The "window == open" condition can never be met while the lock is engaged)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

Definition: A rule execution influences a physical channel (temp, humidity, etc.), which indirectly triggers a subsequent dangerous rule.

Examples: Rule 1: IF temperature_sensor_value < 10°C THEN heater_status = on;Rule 2:IF temperature_sensor_value > 35°C THEN garage_door_status = open. (Rule 1 induces the environment to trigger Rule 2)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Loop
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Loop
Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.
Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Revert
abnormal_type_definition.text:

Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Block

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Mutex
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Mutex
Definition: A single rule contains mutually exclusive logic in its actions, rendering it unstable.
Examples: IF ... THEN curtain_status = closed AND curtain_status = open.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Trigger Mutex
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Trigger Mutex
Definition: A single rule contains mutually exclusive logic in its triggers, rendering it dead.
Examples: IF temperature_sensor_value > 35°C AND temperature_sensor_value < 30°C THEN...
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Condition Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Condition Block
Definition: A rule’s required condition becomes permanently unsatisfiable due to the physical state.
Examples: IF ...THEN window_lock_status = LOCKED; IF Window == OPEN THEN ...(The "window == open" condition can never be met while the lock is engaged)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Privilege Escalation
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Privilege Escalation
Definition: Low-security or non-critical devices triggering high-risk actuators without identity or context verification.
Examples: IF lamp_status == on THEN garage_door_status = open.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.

Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Conflict

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Revert

abnormal_type_definition.title: Implicit Physical Attack (Chaining)
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Implicit Physical Attack (Chaining)
Definition: A rule execution influences a physical channel (temp, humidity, etc.), which indirectly triggers a subsequent dangerous rule.
Dataset Alias: Physical Cross-rule Interaction
Examples: Rule 1: IF temperature_sensor_value < 10°C THEN heater_status = on;Rule 2:IF temperature_sensor_value > 35°C THEN garage_door_status = open. (Rule 1 induces the environment to trigger Rule 2)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Loop
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Loop
Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.
Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Revert
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Revert
Definition: A rule chain where the final action negates the initial rule's intent.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_A = OFF.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Block
Definition: An action cannot execute because a prior rule creates a physical state that denies necessary prerequisites.
Examples: IF ... THEN Water Valve = OFF; IF ... THEN dishwasher = ON. (The action is blocked by no water flow)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Duplication
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Duplication
Definition: Redundant actions triggered on the same device, or an action subsumed by a broader group command.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON AND Device_B = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Conflict
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Conflict
Definition: Multiple rules trigger inconsistent states on the same actuator simultaneously.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Event_X THEN Device_A = OFF.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Privilege Escalation
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Privilege Escalation
Definition: Low-security or non-critical devices triggering high-risk actuators without identity or context verification.
Examples: IF lamp_status == on THEN garage_door_status = open.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Loop
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Loop
Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.
Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Loop
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Loop
Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.
Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Revert
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Revert
Definition: A rule chain where the final action negates the initial rule's intent.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_A = OFF.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Block
Definition: An action cannot execute because a prior rule creates a physical state that denies necessary prerequisites.
Examples: IF ... THEN Water Valve = OFF; IF ... THEN dishwasher = ON. (The action is blocked by no water flow)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Implicit Physical Attack (Chaining)
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Implicit Physical Attack (Chaining)
Definition: A rule execution influences a physical channel (temp, humidity, etc.), which indirectly triggers a subsequent dangerous rule.
Dataset Alias: Physical Cross-rule Interaction
Examples: Rule 1: IF temperature_sensor_value < 10°C THEN heater_status = on;Rule 2:IF temperature_sensor_value > 35°C THEN garage_door_status = open. (Rule 1 induces the environment to trigger Rule 2)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Mutex
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Mutex
Definition: A single rule contains mutually exclusive logic in its actions, rendering it unstable.
Examples: IF ... THEN curtain_status = closed AND curtain_status = open.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Implicit Physical Attack (Chaining)
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Implicit Physical Attack (Chaining)
Definition: A rule execution influences a physical channel (temp, humidity, etc.), which indirectly triggers a subsequent dangerous rule.
Dataset Alias: Physical Cross-rule Interaction
Examples: Rule 1: IF temperature_sensor_value < 10°C THEN heater_status = on;Rule 2:IF temperature_sensor_value > 35°C THEN garage_door_status = open. (Rule 1 induces the environment to trigger Rule 2)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Condition Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Condition Block
Definition: A rule’s required condition becomes permanently unsatisfiable due to the physical state.
Examples: IF ...THEN window_lock_status = LOCKED; IF Window == OPEN THEN ...(The "window == open" condition can never be met while the lock is engaged)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Duplication
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Duplication
Definition: Redundant actions triggered on the same device, or an action subsumed by a broader group command.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON AND Device_B = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

Definition: Redundant actions triggered on the same device, or an action subsumed by a broader group command.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON AND Device_B = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Conflict
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Conflict
Definition: Multiple rules trigger inconsistent states on the same actuator simultaneously.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Event_X THEN Device_A = OFF.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Privilege Escalation
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Privilege Escalation
Definition: Low-security or non-critical devices triggering high-risk actuators without identity or context verification.
Examples: IF lamp_status == on THEN garage_door_status = open.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Condition Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Condition Block
Definition: A rule’s required condition becomes permanently unsatisfiable due to the physical state.
Examples: IF ...THEN window_lock_status = LOCKED; IF Window == OPEN THEN ...(The "window == open" condition can never be met while the lock is engaged)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Implicit Physical Attack (Chaining)
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Implicit Physical Attack (Chaining)
Definition: A rule execution influences a physical channel (temp, humidity, etc.), which indirectly triggers a subsequent dangerous rule.
Dataset Alias: Physical Cross-rule Interaction
Examples: Rule 1: IF temperature_sensor_value < 10°C THEN heater_status = on;Rule 2:IF temperature_sensor_value > 35°C THEN garage_door_status = open. (Rule 1 induces the environment to trigger Rule 2)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Loop
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Loop
Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.
Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Revert
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Revert
Definition: A rule chain where the final action negates the initial rule's intent.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_A = OFF.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

contrastive_guideline.title: Environmental comfort is usually benign
contrastive_guideline.text:
Guideline: Environmental comfort is usually benign
Heating, cooling, fan, humidifier, dehumidifier, purifier, sprinkler, and window actions are normal if thresholds are plausible and actions do not physically block later required conditions.

contrastive_guideline.title: Condition bypass needs missing-constraint evidence
contrastive_guideline.text:
Guideline: Condition bypass needs missing-constraint evidence
A simpler trigger is not automatically a bypass. Mark Condition Bypass only when one rule omits a necessary constraint that another rule establishes as safety- or logic-critical.

contrastive_guideline.title: Same actuator requires simultaneous conflict evidence
contrastive_guideline.text:
Guideline: Same actuator requires simultaneous conflict evidence
Multiple rules controlling the same device attribute are benign when their trigger conditions are mutually exclusive, time-separated, or scenario-specific. Flag only if the rules can fire together and require incompatible states.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Implicit Physical Attack (Chaining)
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Implicit Physical Attack (Chaining)
Definition: A rule execution influences a physical channel (temp, humidity, etc.), which indirectly triggers a subsequent dangerous rule.
Dataset Alias: Physical Cross-rule Interaction
Examples: Rule 1: IF temperature_sensor_value < 10°C THEN heater_status = on;Rule 2:IF temperature_sensor_value > 35°C THEN garage_door_status = open. (Rule 1 induces the environment to trigger Rule 2)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Loop
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Loop
Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.
Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Revert
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Revert
Definition: A rule chain where the final action negates the initial rule's intent.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_A = OFF.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Block
Definition: An action cannot execute because a prior rule creates a physical state that denies necessary prerequisites.
Examples: IF ... THEN Water Valve = OFF; IF ... THEN dishwasher = ON. (The action is blocked by no water flow)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

contrastive_guideline.title: Avoid privacy overthinking
contrastive_guideline.text:
Guideline: Avoid privacy overthinking
Turning on a camera or secure mode from a door, window, motion, smoke, or away-mode signal is usually a security feature, not an anomaly, unless it escalates from an unrelated low-trust trigger to a high-risk actuator.

contrastive_guideline.title: Environmental comfort is usually benign
contrastive_guideline.text:
Guideline: Environmental comfort is usually benign
Heating, cooling, fan, humidifier, dehumidifier, purifier, sprinkler, and window actions are normal if thresholds are plausible and actions do not physically block later required conditions.

contrastive_guideline.title: Same actuator requires simultaneous conflict evidence
contrastive_guideline.text:
Guideline: Same actuator requires simultaneous conflict evidence
Multiple rules controlling the same device attribute are benign when their trigger conditions are mutually exclusive, time-separated, or scenario-specific. Flag only if the rules can fire together and require incompatible states.

contrastive_guideline.title: No evidence means no anomaly

Guideline: Avoid privacy overthinking
Turning on a camera or secure mode from a door, window, motion, smoke, or away-mode signal is usually a security feature, not an anomaly, unless it escalates from an unrelated low-trust trigger to a high-risk actuator.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Condition Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Condition Block
Definition: A rule’s required condition becomes permanently unsatisfiable due to the physical state.
Examples: IF ...THEN window_lock_status = LOCKED; IF Window == OPEN THEN ...(The "window == open" condition can never be met while the lock is engaged)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Implicit Physical Attack (Chaining)
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Implicit Physical Attack (Chaining)
Definition: A rule execution influences a physical channel (temp, humidity, etc.), which indirectly triggers a subsequent dangerous rule.
Dataset Alias: Physical Cross-rule Interaction
Examples: Rule 1: IF temperature_sensor_value < 10°C THEN heater_status = on;Rule 2:IF temperature_sensor_value > 35°C THEN garage_door_status = open. (Rule 1 induces the environment to trigger Rule 2)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Loop
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Loop
Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.
Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Revert
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Revert
Definition: A rule chain where the final action negates the initial rule's intent.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_A = OFF.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

contrastive_guideline.title: Environmental comfort is usually benign
contrastive_guideline.text:
Guideline: Environmental comfort is usually benign
Heating, cooling, fan, humidifier, dehumidifier, purifier, sprinkler, and window actions are normal if thresholds are plausible and actions do not physically block later required conditions.

contrastive_guideline.title: Same actuator requires simultaneous conflict evidence
contrastive_guideline.text:
Guideline: Same actuator requires simultaneous conflict evidence
Multiple rules controlling the same device attribute are benign when their trigger conditions are mutually exclusive, time-separated, or scenario-specific. Flag only if the rules can fire together and require incompatible states.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Loop
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Loop
Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.
Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Condition Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Condition Block
Definition: A rule’s required condition becomes permanently unsatisfiable due to the physical state.
Examples: IF ...THEN window_lock_status = LOCKED; IF Window == OPEN THEN ...(The "window == open" condition can never be met while the lock is engaged)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Revert
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Revert
Definition: A rule chain where the final action negates the initial rule's intent.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_A = OFF.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Loop
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Loop
Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.
Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Conflict
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Conflict
Definition: Multiple rules trigger inconsistent states on the same actuator simultaneously.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Event_X THEN Device_A = OFF.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Revert
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Revert
Definition: A rule chain where the final action negates the initial rule's intent.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_A = OFF.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Block
Definition: An action cannot execute because a prior rule creates a physical state that denies necessary prerequisites.
Examples: IF ... THEN Water Valve = OFF; IF ... THEN dishwasher = ON. (The action is blocked by no water flow)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Loop
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Loop
Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.
Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Privilege Escalation
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Privilege Escalation
Definition: Low-security or non-critical devices triggering high-risk actuators without identity or context verification.
Examples: IF lamp_status == on THEN garage_door_status = open.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Mutex
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Mutex
Definition: A single rule contains mutually exclusive logic in its actions, rendering it unstable.
Examples: IF ... THEN curtain_status = closed AND curtain_status = open.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Condition Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Condition Block
Definition: A rule’s required condition becomes permanently unsatisfiable due to the physical state.
Examples: IF ...THEN window_lock_status = LOCKED; IF Window == OPEN THEN ...(The "window == open" condition can never be met while the lock is engaged)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

contrastive_guideline.title: Environmental comfort is usually benign
contrastive_guideline.text:
Guideline: Environmental comfort is usually benign
Heating, cooling, fan, humidifier, dehumidifier, purifier, sprinkler, and window actions are normal if thresholds are plausible and actions do not physically block later required conditions.

contrastive_guideline.title: Same actuator requires simultaneous conflict evidence
contrastive_guideline.text:
Guideline: Same actuator requires simultaneous conflict evidence
Multiple rules controlling the same device attribute are benign when their trigger conditions are mutually exclusive, time-separated, or scenario-specific. Flag only if the rules can fire together and require incompatible states.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Block

abnormal_type_definition.title: Condition Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Condition Block
Definition: A rule’s required condition becomes permanently unsatisfiable due to the physical state.
Examples: IF ...THEN window_lock_status = LOCKED; IF Window == OPEN THEN ...(The "window == open" condition can never be met while the lock is engaged)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Loop
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Loop
Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.
Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Revert
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Revert
Definition: A rule chain where the final action negates the initial rule's intent.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_A = OFF.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Block
Definition: An action cannot execute because a prior rule creates a physical state that denies necessary prerequisites.
Examples: IF ... THEN Water Valve = OFF; IF ... THEN dishwasher = ON. (The action is blocked by no water flow)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Loop
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Loop
Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.
Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Revert
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Revert
Definition: A rule chain where the final action negates the initial rule's intent.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_A = OFF.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Block
Definition: An action cannot execute because a prior rule creates a physical state that denies necessary prerequisites.
Examples: IF ... THEN Water Valve = OFF; IF ... THEN dishwasher = ON. (The action is blocked by no water flow)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Condition Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Condition Block
Definition: A rule’s required condition becomes permanently unsatisfiable due to the physical state.
Examples: IF ...THEN window_lock_status = LOCKED; IF Window == OPEN THEN ...(The "window == open" condition can never be met while the lock is engaged)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Mutex
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Mutex
Definition: A single rule contains mutually exclusive logic in its actions, rendering it unstable.
Examples: IF ... THEN curtain_status = closed AND curtain_status = open.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Condition Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Condition Block
Definition: A rule’s required condition becomes permanently unsatisfiable due to the physical state.
Examples: IF ...THEN window_lock_status = LOCKED; IF Window == OPEN THEN ...(The "window == open" condition can never be met while the lock is engaged)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Privilege Escalation
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Privilege Escalation
Definition: Low-security or non-critical devices triggering high-risk actuators without identity or context verification.
Examples: IF lamp_status == on THEN garage_door_status = open.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Duplication
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Duplication
Definition: Redundant actions triggered on the same device, or an action subsumed by a broader group command.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON AND Device_B = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Implicit Physical Attack (Chaining)

Anomaly Type: Implicit Physical Attack (Chaining)
Definition: A rule execution influences a physical channel (temp, humidity, etc.), which indirectly triggers a subsequent dangerous rule.

Examples: Rule 1: IF temperature_sensor_value < 10°C THEN heater_status = on;Rule 2:IF temperature_sensor_value > 35°C THEN garage_door_status = open. (Rule 1 induces the environment to trigger Rule 2)

abnormal_type_definition.title: Loop
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Loop
Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.
Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Revert

Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Block

Definition: An action cannot execute because a prior rule creates a physical state that denies necessary prerequisites.
Examples: IF ... THEN Water Valve = OFF; IF ... THEN dishwasher = ON. (The action is blocked by no water flow)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Condition Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Condition Block
Definition: A rule’s required condition becomes permanently unsatisfiable due to the physical state.
Examples: IF ...THEN window_lock_status = LOCKED; IF Window == OPEN THEN ...(The "window == open" condition can never be met while the lock is engaged)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Loop
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Loop
Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.
Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Revert
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Revert
Definition: A rule chain where the final action negates the initial rule's intent.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_A = OFF.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Block
Definition: An action cannot execute because a prior rule creates a physical state that denies necessary prerequisites.
Examples: IF ... THEN Water Valve = OFF; IF ... THEN dishwasher = ON. (The action is blocked by no water flow)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Condition Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Condition Block
Definition: A rule’s required condition becomes permanently unsatisfiable due to the physical state.
Examples: IF ...THEN window_lock_status = LOCKED; IF Window == OPEN THEN ...(The "window == open" condition can never be met while the lock is engaged)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Trigger Mutex
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Trigger Mutex
Definition: A single rule contains mutually exclusive logic in its triggers, rendering it dead.
Examples: IF temperature_sensor_value > 35°C AND temperature_sensor_value < 30°C THEN...
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Duplication
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Duplication
Definition: Redundant actions triggered on the same device, or an action subsumed by a broader group command.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON AND Device_B = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Privilege Escalation
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Privilege Escalation
Definition: Low-security or non-critical devices triggering high-risk actuators without identity or context verification.
Examples: IF lamp_status == on THEN garage_door_status = open.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Condition Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Condition Block
Definition: A rule’s required condition becomes permanently unsatisfiable due to the physical state.
Examples: IF ...THEN window_lock_status = LOCKED; IF Window == OPEN THEN ...(The "window == open" condition can never be met while the lock is engaged)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Loop
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Loop
Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.
Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Implicit Physical Attack (Chaining)
abnormal_type_definition.text:

Definition: A rule execution influences a physical channel (temp, humidity, etc.), which indirectly triggers a subsequent dangerous rule.
Dataset Alias: Physical Cross-rule Interaction
Examples: Rule 1: IF temperature_sensor_value < 10°C THEN heater_status = on;Rule 2:IF temperature_sensor_value > 35°C THEN garage_door_status = open. (Rule 1 induces the environment to trigger Rule 2)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Condition Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Condition Block
Definition: A rule’s required condition becomes permanently unsatisfiable due to the physical state.
Examples: IF ...THEN window_lock_status = LOCKED; IF Window == OPEN THEN ...(The "window == open" condition can never be met while the lock is engaged)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Loop
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Loop
Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.
Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Implicit Physical Attack (Chaining)
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Implicit Physical Attack (Chaining)
Definition: A rule execution influences a physical channel (temp, humidity, etc.), which indirectly triggers a subsequent dangerous rule.
Dataset Alias: Physical Cross-rule Interaction
Examples: Rule 1: IF temperature_sensor_value < 10°C THEN heater_status = on;Rule 2:IF temperature_sensor_value > 35°C THEN garage_door_status = open. (Rule 1 induces the environment to trigger Rule 2)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Revert
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Revert
Definition: A rule chain where the final action negates the initial rule's intent.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_A = OFF.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Implicit Physical Attack (Chaining)
abnormal_type_definition.text:

Examples: Rule 1: IF temperature_sensor_value < 10°C THEN heater_status = on;Rule 2:IF temperature_sensor_value > 35°C THEN garage_door_status = open. (Rule 1 induces the environment to trigger Rule 2)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Implicit Physical Attack (Chaining)
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Implicit Physical Attack (Chaining)
Definition: A rule execution influences a physical channel (temp, humidity, etc.), which indirectly triggers a subsequent dangerous rule.
Dataset Alias: Physical Cross-rule Interaction
Examples: Rule 1: IF temperature_sensor_value < 10°C THEN heater_status = on;Rule 2:IF temperature_sensor_value > 35°C THEN garage_door_status = open. (Rule 1 induces the environment to trigger Rule 2)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Loop
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Loop
Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.
Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Condition Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Condition Block
Definition: A rule’s required condition becomes permanently unsatisfiable due to the physical state.
Examples: IF ...THEN window_lock_status = LOCKED; IF Window == OPEN THEN ...(The "window == open" condition can never be met while the lock is engaged)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Revert
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Revert
Definition: A rule chain where the final action negates the initial rule's intent.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_A = OFF.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

contrastive_guideline.text:
Guideline: Environmental comfort is usually benign
Heating, cooling, fan, humidifier, dehumidifier, purifier, sprinkler, and window actions are normal if thresholds are plausible and actions do not physically block later required conditions.

contrastive_guideline.title: Convenience automation is not automatically anomalous
contrastive_guideline.text:
Guideline: Convenience automation is not automatically anomalous
Motion, door, clock, light, temperature, humidity, and air-quality sensors commonly trigger lights, speakers, curtains, fans, purifiers, humidifiers, or cameras as normal smart-home convenience automation.

contrastive_guideline.title: Same actuator requires simultaneous conflict evidence

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Duplication
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Duplication
Definition: Redundant actions triggered on the same device, or an action subsumed by a broader group command.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON AND Device_B = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Conflict
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Conflict
Definition: Multiple rules trigger inconsistent states on the same actuator simultaneously.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Event_X THEN Device_A = OFF.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Privilege Escalation
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Privilege Escalation
Definition: Low-security or non-critical devices triggering high-risk actuators without identity or context verification.
Examples: IF lamp_status == on THEN garage_door_status = open.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Loop
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Loop
Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.
Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Implicit Physical Attack (Chaining)
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Implicit Physical Attack (Chaining)
Definition: A rule execution influences a physical channel (temp, humidity, etc.), which indirectly triggers a subsequent dangerous rule.
Dataset Alias: Physical Cross-rule Interaction
Examples: Rule 1: IF temperature_sensor_value < 10°C THEN heater_status = on;Rule 2:IF temperature_sensor_value > 35°C THEN garage_door_status = open. (Rule 1 induces the environment to trigger Rule 2)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Loop
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Loop
Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.
Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Revert
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Revert
Definition: A rule chain where the final action negates the initial rule's intent.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_A = OFF.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Block
Definition: An action cannot execute because a prior rule creates a physical state that denies necessary prerequisites.
Examples: IF ... THEN Water Valve = OFF; IF ... THEN dishwasher = ON. (The action is blocked by no water flow)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Trigger Mutex
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Trigger Mutex
Definition: A single rule contains mutually exclusive logic in its triggers, rendering it dead.
Examples: IF temperature_sensor_value > 35°C AND temperature_sensor_value < 30°C THEN...
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Condition Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Condition Block
Definition: A rule’s required condition becomes permanently unsatisfiable due to the physical state.
Examples: IF ...THEN window_lock_status = LOCKED; IF Window == OPEN THEN ...(The "window == open" condition can never be met while the lock is engaged)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Mutex
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Mutex
Definition: A single rule contains mutually exclusive logic in its actions, rendering it unstable.
Examples: IF ... THEN curtain_status = closed AND curtain_status = open.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Loop
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Loop
Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.
Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Revert
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Revert
Definition: A rule chain where the final action negates the initial rule's intent.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_A = OFF.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Condition Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Condition Block
Definition: A rule’s required condition becomes permanently unsatisfiable due to the physical state.
Examples: IF ...THEN window_lock_status = LOCKED; IF Window == OPEN THEN ...(The "window == open" condition can never be met while the lock is engaged)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Block
Definition: An action cannot execute because a prior rule creates a physical state that denies necessary prerequisites.
Examples: IF ... THEN Water Valve = OFF; IF ... THEN dishwasher = ON. (The action is blocked by no water flow)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Loop
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Loop
Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.
Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Condition Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Condition Block
Definition: A rule’s required condition becomes permanently unsatisfiable due to the physical state.
Examples: IF ...THEN window_lock_status = LOCKED; IF Window == OPEN THEN ...(The "window == open" condition can never be met while the lock is engaged)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Implicit Physical Attack (Chaining)
abnormal_type_definition.text:

Dataset Alias: Physical Cross-rule Interaction
Examples: Rule 1: IF temperature_sensor_value < 10°C THEN heater_status = on;Rule 2:IF temperature_sensor_value > 35°C THEN garage_door_status = open. (Rule 1 induces the environment to trigger Rule 2)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Revert
abnormal_type_definition.text:

Definition: A rule chain where the final action negates the initial rule's intent.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_A = OFF.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Duplication
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Duplication
Definition: Redundant actions triggered on the same device, or an action subsumed by a broader group command.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON AND Device_B = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Conflict
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Conflict
Definition: Multiple rules trigger inconsistent states on the same actuator simultaneously.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Event_X THEN Device_A = OFF.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Loop
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Loop
Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.
Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Revert
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Revert
Definition: A rule chain where the final action negates the initial rule's intent.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_A = OFF.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Loop
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Loop
Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.
Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Revert
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Revert
Definition: A rule chain where the final action negates the initial rule's intent.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_A = OFF.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Block
Definition: An action cannot execute because a prior rule creates a physical state that denies necessary prerequisites.
Examples: IF ... THEN Water Valve = OFF; IF ... THEN dishwasher = ON. (The action is blocked by no water flow)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Condition Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Condition Block
Definition: A rule’s required condition becomes permanently unsatisfiable due to the physical state.
Examples: IF ...THEN window_lock_status = LOCKED; IF Window == OPEN THEN ...(The "window == open" condition can never be met while the lock is engaged)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Loop
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Loop
Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.
Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Conflict
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Conflict
Definition: Multiple rules trigger inconsistent states on the same actuator simultaneously.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Event_X THEN Device_A = OFF.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Revert
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Revert
Definition: A rule chain where the final action negates the initial rule's intent.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_A = OFF.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Block
Definition: An action cannot execute because a prior rule creates a physical state that denies necessary prerequisites.
Examples: IF ... THEN Water Valve = OFF; IF ... THEN dishwasher = ON. (The action is blocked by no water flow)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

contrastive_guideline.title: Environmental comfort is usually benign
contrastive_guideline.text:
Guideline: Environmental comfort is usually benign
Heating, cooling, fan, humidifier, dehumidifier, purifier, sprinkler, and window actions are normal if thresholds are plausible and actions do not physically block later required conditions.

contrastive_guideline.title: Same actuator requires simultaneous conflict evidence
contrastive_guideline.text:
Guideline: Same actuator requires simultaneous conflict evidence
Multiple rules controlling the same device attribute are benign when their trigger conditions are mutually exclusive, time-separated, or scenario-specific. Flag only if the rules can fire together and require incompatible states.

contrastive_guideline.title: Avoid privacy overthinking
contrastive_guideline.text:
Guideline: Avoid privacy overthinking
Turning on a camera or secure mode from a door, window, motion, smoke, or away-mode signal is usually a security feature, not an anomaly, unless it escalates from an unrelated low-trust trigger to a high-risk actuator.

Anomaly Type: Safety Boundary Error
Definition: Thresholds that exceed physical safety limits or device operating ranges.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Condition Block
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Condition Block
Definition: A rule’s required condition becomes permanently unsatisfiable due to the physical state.
Examples: IF ...THEN window_lock_status = LOCKED; IF Window == OPEN THEN ...(The "window == open" condition can never be met while the lock is engaged)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Implicit Physical Attack (Chaining)
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Implicit Physical Attack (Chaining)
Definition: A rule execution influences a physical channel (temp, humidity, etc.), which indirectly triggers a subsequent dangerous rule.
Dataset Alias: Physical Cross-rule Interaction
Examples: Rule 1: IF temperature_sensor_value < 10°C THEN heater_status = on;Rule 2:IF temperature_sensor_value > 35°C THEN garage_door_status = open. (Rule 1 induces the environment to trigger Rule 2)
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

Definition: Rules that contradict basic physical laws or safety heuristics, leading to property damage.

Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

Anomaly Type: Action Duplication
Definition: Redundant actions triggered on the same device, or an action subsumed by a broader group command.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON AND Device_B = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Action Conflict
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Action Conflict
Definition: Multiple rules trigger inconsistent states on the same actuator simultaneously.
Examples: IF Event_X THEN Device_A = ON; IF Event_X THEN Device_A = OFF.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Privilege Escalation
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Privilege Escalation
Definition: Low-security or non-critical devices triggering high-risk actuators without identity or context verification.
Examples: IF lamp_status == on THEN garage_door_status = open.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.

abnormal_type_definition.title: Loop
abnormal_type_definition.text:
Anomaly Type: Loop
Definition: Causal dependencies between rules form a closed loop, leading to infinite state oscillation.
Examples: IF Device_A == ON THEN Device_B = OFF; IF Device_B == OFF THEN Device_A = ON.
Diagnosis cue: only mark this type when the current rules contain direct logical evidence.
